common_mistakes.mistake: Both heroes leave a recoil tissue together, or the intended launcher steps away before both are jointly supported.
common_mistakes.consequence: No single remaining supported hero receives the recoil launch, so the high crossing may fail and one or both heroes can drop to the safe floor.
common_mistakes.recovery: Regroup on the broad safe floor and return to the tissue; the room does not reset merely for landing below.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assume the moving fold is stationary or try to jump from it while its position is inconvenient.
common_mistakes.consequence: The fold’s location changes, delaying the lower crossing; the full-width safe floor remains underneath.

confidence_reason: Authored mechanics and one ordinary-input completion establish feasible causal routes, passive moving-fold behavior, safe-floor recovery, and separate exits. They do not establish whether first-time players discover the handoffs, how consistently they recover, or human control friction.

confirmed: The subtitle and exit layout genuinely cue a partner launch and vertically separated goals. The high/low route split is real.
missed_mechanics: Recoil tissues launch the remaining hero only after both were jointly supported at the start of a substep; the two tissues implement two sequential handoffs.
A full-width safe floor underlies the crossings, so the visible gaps do not imply mandatory lethal exposure.
The lower fold moves horizontally and carries riders; distinct sparks are owner-specific optional objectives.
The third idle frame records automatic bubble impact, FLOAT, and displaced heroes; it does not establish player-caused feedback.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass grouped all folds as unknown and left route connectivity unresolved; source shows a designed upper-shelf/lower-moving-fold split joined at the second tissue.
The first pass assigned hazards 2 from gaps/lower tissue without consequence evidence; the authored full-width floor and empty hazard list support 0 on the mandatory route.
The first pass treated any partner-bounce as an unspecified action; source identifies a precise remaining-supported recoil trigger and the intended actor order.
changed_judgments: Reasoning remains 3 because the cue gives the broad strategy but not the causal launch condition; the two ordered handoffs and split routes confirm several dependent decisions.
Cooperation remains 3, now supported by two mandatory complementary handoffs rather than merely presumed partner bounce.
Execution decreases 3 to 2 because ordinary-input route evidence reaches both exits with controlled but forgiving traversal; no scarce landing margin is evidenced.
Timing changes from unknown to 1 because the moving fold is continuous rather than a timed gate, and tissue handoffs depend on support state rather than a narrow clock window.
Hazards decreases 2 to 0 because the whole-width safe floor and absence of authored hazards remove the inferred lethal gap exposure.
Novelty decreases 3 to 2: bubbles and moving lift/split-route ideas were previously cued; the recoil handoff is the principal new causal combination.
Recovery changes from unknown to 1 because safe-floor regrouping and the explicit source hint allow another attempt without a mandatory death/reset.
Solution clarity remains burden 2: the high-road cue is clear, while the recoil trigger and order remain unstated. Control friction remains unknown.
unresolved: The room’s idle third-frame bubble hit is visible but not player-caused; exact timing/trajectory for a human trying to exploit or avoid it is not measured.
No human novice route, recovery behavior, time, enjoyment, or difficulty distribution was observed.
The route receipt records 2/2 sparks but does not attribute pickup to individual intervals; collecting sparks remains optional.

single_operator_note: A one-person player must switch attention between A/D/W and arrows while arranging two sequential support handoffs and separate exits. The accepted scripted route does not measure this additional coordination burden.
